title: Birth in Red Bank and his first teacher Grace Mowchow
summary: Basie confirms his birth in Red Bank, New Jersey in 1904; his mother got him started but Grace Mowchow was his real teacher, starting with scales.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: All righty. So, Leonard Feather's (PHONETIC) Encyclopedia of Jazz says that you were born in Red Bank, New Jersey on August 21st, 1904. That's true?
That's true, okay, and that you studied music with your mother.
I wonder, you know, if you could comment on that.
She sort of got me started, but my real music teacher was Grace [Mowchow.]
Was she a friend of your mother's?
Yeah, not a friend, but she was a music teacher.
She was a music teacher. She was the one that I took my music lessons from.
Okay, we were back with Grace Mowchow? (PHONETIC).
Could you tell me what she taught you? Was she a piano teacher?
Yeah, I mean, took lessons like anyone that's starting, just starting.
What did you start with? I mean, different teachers have different, you know, methods.
(Inaudible) first started, I think we just started with scales and things like that (inaudible). I can't go into too much detail there.
Because I don't remember all those things.
Do you remember your first music book?

No. No, I don't. I'll tell you the truth, I wasn't that interested really, (inaudible), because I had to (inaudible) taught me how to read (inaudible). That much of it, you know, I didn't finish. I didn't (Inaudible) go through like -- I just really didn't (inaudible).
Well, what did your mother taught you, if Grace Mowchow taught you scales?

Well, I don't know -- see, my mother wasn't really -- I can just tell you, actually (inaudible). She just got me interested in, you know, playing. As far as actually teaching (inaudible), you know. But she could kind of play a little bit, you know. And not the, you know, cradle hymn things now, and she never actually taught me any lessons, you know.
